sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: The front matter of a 2011 WHO, UNFPA, UNAIDS and IPPF case study from Swaziland on linking sexual and reproductive health with HIV/AIDS services, in support of the Global Plan to eliminate new HIV infections among children. It contains the title pages, copyright and disclaimer notice with publisher contact details, acknowledgements of Swazi and international partner organizations and main contributors, and the table of contents.

sections.title: Prongs 1 and 2 – programming of elimination of mother-to-child transmission

summary.text: Defines the distinction between linkages and integration of sexual and reproductive health and HIV services, and notes a shift in global attention from preventing mother-to-child transmission alone towards recognizing links between maternal health, HIV and child survival under the Millennium Development Goals.

sections.extract: programming of elimination of mother-to-child transmission Key definitions In delineating the full scope of a linked SRH and HIV response, the following distinction has been made between linkages and integration:2 Linkages Bi-directional (two-way) synergies in policy, programmes, services and advocacy between SRH and HIV. This is a broad, human rights-based approach, of which service integration is a sub-set.

sections.title: The commitment towards elimination of new HIV infections among children by 2015 and keeping their mothers alive

summary.text: Explains the global commitment to eliminate new HIV infections among children by 2015 while keeping mothers alive, built on four prongs of comprehensive programming integrated with sexual and reproductive health. It highlights growing attention to the first two prongs, preventing HIV in women and preventing unintended pregnancies among women living with HIV. Tables set out the prongs and associated interventions such as family planning, blood safety, stigma reduction and prevention of gender-based violence.

sections.title: Background

summary.text: Describes the background to Swaziland's HIV epidemic, noting the world's highest adult HIV prevalence, very low life expectancy and a high proportion of pregnant women living with HIV. It closes with a statement by the Prime Minister to the UN General Assembly committing the country to reduce new infections among children to zero by 2015.

sections.extract: Swaziland is known for having the highest rate of adult HIV infection in the world, with a recent figure at 25.9%.14 Swaziland is also one of 22 low- and middle-income priority countries15 with the highest estimated numbers of pregnant women living with HIV. sections.title: Case study sites

summary.text: Profiles the case study sites in Swaziland, starting with the Family Life Association of Swaziland and its youth-friendly clinics offering integrated sexual and reproductive health and HIV services, alongside other service providers mapped across the country. It then documents promising practices addressing Prong 1, preventing HIV among women, and Prong 2, preventing unintended pregnancies among women living with HIV. The section covers community outreach, peer education, counselling, family planning and linked referral services. It ends with a checklist of questions that facilities can use to assess whether they provide these services and have built them into standard operating procedures.

tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Table 1: The four prongs for comprehensive programming
rows: Prevention of HIV among women of reproductive age within services related to reproductive health, such as antenatal care, post-partum and post-natal care and other health and HIV service delivery points, including working with community structures.

Providing appropriate counselling and support, and contraceptives, to women living with HIV, to meet their unmet needs for family planning and spacing of births, and to optimize health outcomes for these women and their children.

For pregnant women living with HIV, ensuring HIV testing and counselling, and access to the antiretroviral (ARV) drugs needed to prevent HIV infection from being passed on to their babies during pregnancy, delivery and breastfeeding.
HIV care, treatment and support for women and children living with HIV, and for their families.

narratives.en: The table describes the four prongs of comprehensive programming for the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV: primary prevention of HIV among women of reproductive age, prevention of unintended pregnancies among women living with HIV, prevention of HIV transmission to babies, and care, treatment and support for women and children living with HIV and their families.

narratives.ru: В таблице описаны четыре направления комплексной программы элиминации передачи ВИЧ от матери ребёнку: первичная профилактика ВИЧ среди женщин репродуктивного возраста, предотвращение незапланированной беременности у женщин, живущих с ВИЧ, предотвращение передачи ВИЧ детям, а также уход, лечение и поддержка для женщин и детей, живущих с ВИЧ, и их семей.

tables.label: Table 4
tables.caption: Table 4: Checklist for services that support Prong 1
rows: 1. Consider your community- and facility-based health education activities, aimed at both young and adult women, and their partners. Are these activities conducted to increase awareness about (a) the advantages and (b) the availability of the following services to:
support informed decision-making about sexual debut, the risks of HIV transmission and the use of contraception, including condoms?
support consistent use of male or female condoms to prevent HIV transmission, other STIs, and unintended pregnancy?
encourage uptake of voluntary counselling and testing in order to determine their HIV status?
encourage the early treatment of sexually transmitted infections?

2. Are these activities and services provided in an adolescent- or youth-friendly manner? Do they attempt to address – even in a partial way – the structural factors that increase women’s vulnerability to HIV, such as:
gender inequality?
multiple concurrent partnerships?
violence against women?
HIV-related stigma and discrimination?
3. Are women who have experienced gender-based violence routinely provided with:
counselling support and related SRH services?
psychosocial and legal support?
emergency contraception in the event of a sexual assault?
post-exposure prophylaxis in the event of a sexual assault?
4. For those women who are pregnant, have tested HIV-negative and are attending antenatal, or post-partum care services, are they routinely:
provided with information and counselling on safer sex, risk reduction and condom use during the course of their pregnancy and the post-partum period?
provided with information and counselling on STI prevention (including information on the recognition of symptoms) and, where necessary, the treatment of STIs?
encouraged and supported to involve their male partner in their antenatal and post-natal care consultations?
provided with the contraceptives of choice in preparation for post-partum sexual activity and, importantly, provided with condoms during their antenatal care consultations?

provided with an opportunity to discuss the issue of post-partum sexual activity and contraception early after delivery or even late in the last trimester to provide women with the appropriate knowledge to allow them to make informed decisions regarding their reproductive futures?
encouraged to re-test for HIV on a regular basis throughout and after their pregnancy – ideally with their partner in the context of a couple counselling session?
5. Are contraceptive commodities and, importantly, male and female condoms, readily available to women at every consultation they have with a health service provider?
6. Are creative strategies used by health care providers to encourage greater male involvement in antenatal, maternity and post-partum care such as:
educational talks?
an invitation to attend a medical consultation without waiting in line?
couple counselling?

7. Are health care providers, with a woman’s consent, able to skilfully address male partners in such a way as to raise awareness of their responsibility for practising safer sex and facilitate the associated behaviour change?
8. To ensure the components of Prong 1 are integrated into routine practice within the facility and organization:
are all members of the health team sufficiently trained to provide the above interventions with their clients?

has the team agreed at which points in the PMTCT process (i.e. provider-initiated HIV testing and counselling, antenatal care, intrapartum care, post-natal care, and follow-up of HIV-exposed infants) the above information and counselling will be provided to clients?
has the health team identified which members of the health team will provide clients with the above information and services?

are the above elements incorporated into standard operating procedures or guidelines of the facility or organization, so that all (and specifically new) members of the health team are aware of this practice?
tables.notes: The Y, N and I columns are blank tick boxes in the printed checklist. The “Question” header spans the first two columns.

narratives.en: The table is a self-assessment checklist of eight questions, most with sub-items, for health services supporting Prong 1 (primary HIV prevention among women), covering health education, youth-friendly services, gender-based violence, care for HIV-negative pregnant women, condom availability, male involvement and integration into routine practice. Each item has blank Y, N and I boxes to tick.
narratives.ar: الجدول قائمة تحقق للتقييم الذاتي تتضمن ثمانية أسئلة، معظمها ببنود فرعية، للخدمات الصحية الداعمة للمحور 1 (الوقاية الأولية من فيروس العوز المناعي البشري بين النساء)، وتشمل التثقيف الصحي، والخدمات الملائمة للشباب، والعنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي، ورعاية الحوامل السلبيات للفيروس، وتوافر العوازل، وإشراك الرجال، والإدماج في الممارسة الروتينية. ولكل بند خانات فارغة Y وN وI للتأشير.
narratives.zh: 本表是一份自我评估核对清单，包含八个问题（多数含子项），供支持第1方面（妇女艾滋病毒初级预防）的卫生服务使用，涵盖健康教育、青年友好服务、基于性别的暴力、艾滋病毒阴性孕妇的保健、安全套供应、男性参与以及纳入常规做法。每个条目设有空白的Y、N、I勾选框。
narratives.es: El cuadro es una lista de verificación de autoevaluación con ocho preguntas, la mayoría con subapartados, para los servicios de salud que apoyan el eje 1 (prevención primaria del VIH en mujeres), que abarca la educación sanitaria, los servicios adaptados a los jóvenes, la violencia de género, la atención a embarazadas VIH-negativas, la disponibilidad de preservativos, la participación masculina y la integración en la práctica habitual. Cada elemento tiene casillas Y, N e I en blanco.
narratives.fr: Le tableau est une liste de contrôle d’auto-évaluation de huit questions, la plupart avec des sous-points, destinée aux services de santé soutenant le volet 1 (prévention primaire du VIH chez les femmes) : éducation sanitaire, services adaptés aux jeunes, violence sexiste, prise en charge des femmes enceintes séronégatives, disponibilité des préservatifs, participation des hommes et intégration dans la pratique courante. Chaque point comporte des cases Y, N et I vides.
narratives.ru: Таблица представляет собой контрольный перечень для самооценки из восьми вопросов, большинство с подпунктами, для медицинских служб, поддерживающих направление 1 (первичная профилактика ВИЧ среди женщин): санитарное просвещение, услуги, ориентированные на молодёжь, гендерное насилие, помощь ВИЧ-отрицательным беременным, доступность презервативов, участие мужчин и включение в повседневную практику. Для каждого пункта предусмотрены пустые графы Y, N и I.

tables.label: Table 5
tables.caption: Table 5: Checklist for services that support Prong 2
rows: 1. Do women living with HIV also receive, as part of their routine HIV services, SRH counselling which:
affirms the right of women living with HIV, and couples, to make an informed decision about whether and when they want children?
provides women with information on the healthy timing and spacing of pregnancies?

focuses, on a regular basis, on fertility intentions – and if a pregnancy is desired, is a client provided with the necessary pre-conception counselling and care so as to plan for conception in a way that optimizes her health, that of her partner (particularly in the case of a sero-discordant couple) and prevents MTCT?

provides information, in a non-judgmental manner, on the full range of contraceptive options available to women, their use and side effects, and how a client can access the commodity of their choice at the service delivery site – including the availability of and access to emergency contraception?

discusses the value of dual protection and provides the client with skills-building support to reduce unprotected sex (and, for example, introduce the use of condoms into her existing and future sexual relationships)?

discusses the involvement and joint responsibility of the client’s male partner in practising safer sex, contraception and planning for conception – and considers ways the client can encourage his involvement in these issues in the future?
provides information and counselling on STI prevention (including information on the recognition of symptoms) and, where necessary, the treatment of STIs?
provides support for HIV disclosure, particularly in sero-discordant couples?
2. If a support group for people living with HIV is convened, are the above sexual and reproductive health and rights issues similarly raised and discussed as part of the content of this group?

3. Are members of the health team equipped to provide counselling and support for perinatally infected adolescents who, increasingly, will require similar information and services related to family planning and dual protection, pre-conception care and PMTCT?
4. Are contraceptive commodities and, importantly, male and female condoms readily available to women living with HIV at every consultation they have with a health service provider?
5. Are women living with HIV, who have experienced gender-based violence, routinely provided with:
counselling, psychosocial and legal support?
emergency contraception and other related services in the event of a sexual assault?
6. To ensure the components of Prong 2 are integrated into routine practice within the facility and organization:
are all members of the health team sufficiently trained to provide the above interventions with their clients?

has the team agreed at which points in the PMTCT process (i.e. provider-initiated HIV testing and counselling, antenatal care, intrapartum care, post-natal care, and follow-up of exposed infants) the above information and counselling will be provided to clients?
has the health team identified which members of the health team will provide clients with the above information and services?

are the above elements incorporated into standard operating procedures or guidelines of the facility or organization so that all (and specifically new) members of the health team are aware of this practice?
tables.notes: The Y, N and I columns are blank tick boxes in the printed checklist. The “Question” header spans the first two columns. In question 1, the question cell spans only the first three sub-items; the left cells of the remaining five sub-items are printed empty.

narratives.en: The table is a self-assessment checklist of six questions, several with sub-items, for health services supporting Prong 2 (preventing unintended pregnancies in women living with HIV), covering SRH counselling within HIV services, support groups, perinatally infected adolescents, contraceptive availability, gender-based violence and integration into routine practice. Each item has blank Y, N and I boxes to tick.
narratives.ar: الجدول قائمة تحقق للتقييم الذاتي تتضمن ستة أسئلة، بعضها ببنود فرعية، للخدمات الصحية الداعمة للمحور 2 (منع الحمل غير المقصود لدى النساء المتعايشات مع فيروس العوز المناعي البشري)، وتشمل مشورة الصحة الجنسية والإنجابية ضمن خدمات الفيروس، ومجموعات الدعم، والمراهقين المصابين في الفترة المحيطة بالولادة، وتوافر وسائل منع الحمل، والعنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي، والإدماج في الممارسة الروتينية. ولكل بند خانات فارغة Y وN وI للتأشير.
narratives.zh: 本表是一份自我评估核对清单，包含六个问题（部分含子项），供支持第2方面（预防艾滋病毒感染妇女意外怀孕）的卫生服务使用，涵盖艾滋病毒服务中的性与生殖健康咨询、支持小组、围产期感染青少年、避孕药具供应、基于性别的暴力以及纳入常规做法。每个条目设有空白的Y、N、I勾选框。
narratives.es: El cuadro es una lista de verificación de autoevaluación con seis preguntas, varias con subapartados, para los servicios de salud que apoyan el eje 2 (prevención de embarazos no deseados en mujeres con VIH), que abarca el asesoramiento en SSR dentro de los servicios de VIH, los grupos de apoyo, los adolescentes con infección perinatal, la disponibilidad de anticonceptivos, la violencia de género y la integración en la práctica habitual. Cada elemento tiene casillas Y, N e I en blanco.
narratives.fr: Le tableau est une liste de contrôle d’auto-évaluation de six questions, plusieurs avec des sous-points, destinée aux services de santé soutenant le volet 2 (prévention des grossesses non désirées chez les femmes vivant avec le VIH) : conseil en SSR dans les services VIH, groupes de soutien, adolescents infectés en période périnatale, disponibilité des contraceptifs, violence sexiste et intégration dans la pratique courante. Chaque point comporte des cases Y, N et I vides.
narratives.ru: Таблица представляет собой контрольный перечень для самооценки из шести вопросов, часть которых имеет подпункты, для медицинских служб, поддерживающих направление 2 (предотвращение незапланированной беременности у женщин, живущих с ВИЧ): консультирование по СРЗ в рамках услуг по ВИЧ, группы поддержки, подростки с перинатальной инфекцией, доступность контрацептивов, гендерное насилие и включение в повседневную практику. Для каждого пункта предусмотрены пустые графы Y, N и I.
